draft.title: Job analysis
card: Job analysis is the study of a job to find out what it involves. A business may watch workers, interview them or ask them to fill in a survey.
The findings are used for job design, which is deciding what tasks a job includes and how they fit together.
a list of the duties of the job, such as what tasks are done and who the worker reports to.
a list of the skills, knowledge, qualifications and experience a person needs to do the job well.
draft.remember: Job analysis studies the job. The description lists the duties. The specification lists what the person needs.

a.q: Which item belongs in a job specification for a bakery assistant?
opts: A food safety certificate and experience using ovens
Opening the shop, serving customers and cleaning up
Reporting to the head baker each morning
Studying how the bakery assistants spend their shifts
a.why: A job specification lists what a person needs to do the job, such as qualifications and experience. Serving customers and reporting to the head baker are duties and reporting lines, so they belong in the job description.
a.clue: Which one describes the person, not the tasks?

b.q: Priya manages a gym in Geelong. She watches the front desk staff for a week, then lists the qualifications she wants in a new hire. What did she do?
opts: Job analysis, then a job specification
Job analysis, then a job description
Job design, then a job specification
Job specification, then a job analysis
b.why: Watching staff to learn what the job involves is job analysis. A list of the qualifications a person needs is a job specification. A job description would list duties, not qualifications, and the study must come before the documents.
b.clue: Studying comes first. Then ask whether the list names duties or person needs.

a.best: A food safety certificate and experience using ovens

b.best: Job analysis, then a job specification
